panpipes noun

also pan flute, pipes of Pan, shepherd’s pipe, syrinx

classical

Verg. Ecl. 2.32–37
Tib. 2.5.31
Ov. M. 1.688

fistula, fistulae f.

noun, first declension

Any pipe or tube, and in particular the shepherd’s pipe of reeds of falling length, Pan’s invention; Traupman (168) has it for any pipe.

Examples

  • fistula, cui semper dēcrēscit arundinis ōrdō: nam calamus cērā jungitur usque minor

    the pipe, in which the row of reeds keeps growing shorter: for each reed is joined with wax to a smaller oneTib. 2.5.31–32 (Lewis & Short)

  • Opiliō (pāstor) pāscit gregem, īnstrūctus fistulā et pērā, ut et pedō

    The shepherd feeds his flock, equipped with a pipe and a bag, and a crook tooComen. OP 46

See also flute, recorder, musical instrument.

SourcesLewis & Short: fistula

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 168.

Comenius from the Latinitas loci collection (loci-comenius).
